artifacts.summary: 8-phase, 10.75-hour plan splitting MintBound.lean (15,684 lines) into 18 modules behind a retained aggregator, with de-privatization isolated to one phase and five batched build gates.

memory_candidates.content: Decomposing an oversized Lean 4 module: the binding constraint is `private` visibility, which is module-scoped in Lean 4 -- a private name does not cross a module boundary, and the usual failure mode is not a build error at the cut but a temptation to duplicate the proof (BimodalLogic already carries `pick_split'`/`pick_splitOrdered'` in MintBound.lean solely because Fuel.lean's originals are private). The reusable planning recipe: (1) run a whole-file name cross-product restricted to code lines to derive the cross-boundary private set BEFORE proposing any cut; (2) verify file order IS dependency order by checking for zero forward references -- if true, file order is the only acyclic cut and thematic groupings are usually cyclic (measure this rather than assuming); (3) grep the whole tree for collisions before de-privatizing, since short helper names like `fwp`/`mfp`/`mwE` are collision-prone; (4) check for file-scoped `set_option` and `open` lines, which must be replicated into every extracted module, versus per-declaration `set_option ... in` forms, which travel with their declaration; (5) confirm no `section ... end` block straddles a proposed cut. Extraction must proceed TOP-DOWN (head first), because the residual file imports the extracted prefix; extracting the tail first creates an import cycle. A pure-prose tail section is the exception and can go first.
